people.gloss: The nine bends of the river
people.role: Ferry master of Lãng Đào Môn since 1010: the nine landings, the river tolls and the rebuilt fleet
people.appearance: A barrel of a man with a river-boatman's tan and a voice that carries across three bends, who wears the toll seal on a cord round his wrist.
people.backstory: Giang Cửu Khúc was born on a ferry at Hoành Độ Thôn in 880 and named for the river. He poled boats before he could read, and learned the Nine Bends Art from the founder Uông Liên Chu (uong_lien_chu), who had made one gate out of the feuding boat families after Phá Chu Trấn burned (V047). He took the gate in 1010 and has kept the nine landings since. He made the gate rich on tolls. In 1172 the tolls on the Ngư Ca border started a war (C192). The next year Lạc Hà's raiders burned his fleet at the Đào Sa landing (A080), and his ferrymen burned with it, Lữ Thừa Lãng (lu_thua_lang) among them. The pines fought for him and took no land, and Dụ Tĩnh Lưu (du_tinh_luu) split the tolls with Lạc Hà in 1175 and rebuilt his boats with the River Hall's timber. Every spring since, he has written to Lữ's son, whom Lạc Hà raised, and asked him to come home. Lữ Tẫn Chu (lu_tan_chu) has not come.
people.wants: Lữ Tẫn Chu home on a Lãng Đào ferry, the fleet back to its old size, and the Ngư Ca tolls whole again.
people.secret: The toll quarrel that started the Ferry War was his. For ten years before 1172 he charged Lạc Hà's boats at the Ngư Ca landing a toll the pines never set, and kept it. The pines went to war for his greed and he let them believe it was for his honour.

people.role: Mistress of the boats: the fleet, its building and its crews; saved the one ferry that did not burn
people.appearance: A tall helmsman's daughter with white hair cropped like a deckhand's and a burn across both palms.
people.backstory: Born in Đà Công Thôn, the helmsmen's village, she has been Giang Cửu Khúc's (giang_cuu_khuc) Dao partner since 1040 and mistress of the boats since 1100. On the night Lạc Hà fired the Đào Sa landing (A080) she cut one ferry loose and poled it into the current with nine children aboard, and its sail is her flag now. She rebuilt the fleet with the River Hall's timber in 1175. She does not know why the war began, and she has started reading the old toll books.

people.role: The ferry master's son and heir; captain of the Đào Sa landing
people.appearance: His father's build and his mother's burned hands, and a half-healed scar where a Lạc Hà oar took him in 1173.
people.backstory: He was on the Đào Sa landing in 1173 (A080) when the boats burned and has captained it since. He wants the Ferry War fought again and won, and he says so to Đặng Hoành Giang (dang_hoanh_giang), the pines' man at the gate, whenever the River Hall is listening. His daughter Giang Tiểu Loan (giang_tieu_loan) is his disciple. He thinks his father's letters to Lữ Tẫn Chu are weakness.

people.role: Founder of Lãng Đào Môn (790); made one gate of the feuding boat families
people.backstory: Born in Phá Chu Trấn, he saw it burned in the landing feud of 786 (V047) and Phân Thủy Môn's boats sunk two years later (V048). In 790 he lashed the surviving families' boats together across the river and would not untie them until they swore one gate under the pines (A075). He wrote the Washing Waves Canon from their songs and cut the toll seal, and he taught Giang Cửu Khúc (giang_cuu_khuc).
